Sometimes they are proctored, which means that you have to film yourself and share a screen recording so that they can ensure it’s you taking the test and that you are not using prohibited aids. In essence, they are similar to programming interviews, just with automated tests and no interviewer present. Programming Interview Programming interviews are the core of the software and ML engineering interview process, and they have been part of every interview process I’ve encountered. They come in several different forms, which we discuss shortly. But first, talk about general advice. They all serve a common goal: to evaluate how you think, break down a problem, think about edge cases, and work toward the solution of a programming problem. In the process, companies want to see your communication and collaboration skills. To that end, it’s imperative that you talk out loud. I think it’s fine to read the exercise and think for a minute in silence, but after that, I was verbalizing my thought process to give the interviewer enough signal to judge my ability beyond a binary pass/fail of the task. Sometimes, the Interviewers gave me hints or helped me to avoid exploring an impasse. Of course, it’s better to pass without any interventions, but it’s a lot better to get the code to work with help than not work at all. If I were stuck, I would try to explain where and why. Sometimes that was enough to figure out a solution myself, but it also presented a possibility for the interviewer to nudge me in the right direction. Let’s now discuss the different kinds of programming interviews in more detail. Leetcode Type Interview The most common coding interview questions are LeetCode or LeetCode-style questions that are adapted to the domain in which the company operates. In all these interviews, I was asked to share my screen. Sometimes using my own editor, sometimes coding in Google Docs, but most often in a Coderpad online interpreter. Whenever there was an interpreter, we ran my code against tests. If they failed, I used the test output for debugging. Generally, it helped to think through the problem first and get buy-in for a high-level pseudo-code solution written out in comments before writing out the actual code. If I could choose the language for the interview, I would choose Python. Partly because it’s a language I’m pretty well versed in, but also because I didn’t want to deal with memory issues in an algorithmic interview. Generally, I would recommend going for a high-level language that you are familiar with. There is little value in wrestling with the borrow checker or forgetting to declare a variable when you could just use Python and focus on the algorithm. There are many resources to prepare for these types of interviews, and getting good at them is pretty much a practice and pattern recognition thing. You build a repertoire of algorithmic techniques and useful data structures and their operations, and with time, develop expertise to mix and match to a solution quickly. I found the Neetcode 150 roadmap particularly useful. It’s an ordered collection of LeetCode problems that one after the other introduce new and more advanced concepts. I found that much more useful than the arbitrary order of LeetCode. Because I am a big believer in more rigorous (self-)education, I’ve also read Skiena’s Algorithm Design Manual. This is probably a bit too theoretical for immediate interview preparation, but it is a great base for your life as a programmer. For more conceptual coding interview preparation, I’ve supplemented this with reading Coding Interview Patterns — a practical and interview-focused approach to data structures and algorithms. In the end, I’ve probably done around 300 LeetCode/NeetCode problems. About half of that is to build muscle memory, and then 20-30 rapid-fire questions in the days leading up to the coding interviews. The interviews themselves consisted usually of two or three problems, with the first one or two being equivalent to a LeetCode easy as a warm-up, followed mostly by a LeetCode medium, though I’ve encountered hards. The most effective means of preparation was just practice to get a solid base, supplemented with several mock interviews with friends, where we role-played to get comfortable talking aloud when coding up a solution. It also helped to get a couple of real interviews under my belt. I was considerably less nervous in the later ones. API/System Design Coding Interview I’ve had some coding interviews that had much more of an API or system design focus. These are different from the typical system design interview conducted on a whiteboard in that I was expected to produce code. They did not concern themselves with the design of a scalable and fault-tolerant distributed system. For example, I had to design the method interfaces of a BankingSystem class or design a program to sort a text file many times larger than the memory of the machine on which it was run. These interviews didn’t have tests, and partly, pseudocode was accepted. Here, I often did not need to fully implement the solution, but had to talk through my rationale with the interviewers, often with the help of pseudocode we were writing in a notepad. The best means of preparation for these interviews was building a couple of larger-scale projects, which made me encounter similar issues in the wild, and building a sufficient theoretical computer science foundation to understand the problems and trade-offs. Real-world challenge Sometimes, a programming interview is made to mimic a real-world challenge that resembles work you may have at the job. For example, wrangling a messy real-world dataset or implementing a Lambda function that calls an LLM API to scrape certain information from a given website and saves it to a database. One of these interviews allowed me to use LLM assistance and was pretty much judged on completion speed. I did pretty poorly because at the time, I was actively avoiding AI-assisted coding to build muscle memory in Rust syntax, and hence, I was slow and clunky using the LLM. I don’t think I’ve had enough of these interviews to make any generalizable recommendations. System Design Interview System design interviews serve to gauge your exposure to creating software that solves a business problem while satisfying preset constraints on the load it must be able to handle, as well as its fault tolerance. They are usually open-ended, and the design is iteratively created in a discussion with the interviewer. As with the coding interviews, it is important that you communicate throughout the interview to make sure your interviewer understands how you are thinking about trade-offs. Speaking out loud also helps them to course correct you if you make an assumption that is not warranted. While it is some work to prepare for system design interviews, there are some great and helpful resources out there. Martin Kleppman’s Designing Data Intensive Applications covers handling of data from storing it on a single machine, space-efficiently sending it around, to distributed consensus algorithms to gracefully handle network partitions. It took me about six months to work through it while having it on my bedside table. While it’s more than what you need for a single interview, and you definitely don’t need to know everything by heart for interviewing, I believe there are great dividends for your software or ML engineering career. Plus, if you’ve read DDIA, you have the theoretical foundation to go deep on your design decisions. For more practical and interview-focused preparation, I’ve read Alex Xu’s System Design Interview. It covers a couple of reference system designs, gives interview tactics, and contains example system schemas. It’s not that long and a fast and easy read, especially compared to DDIA. Another useful reference was the System Design Primer GitHub repository, which contains additional example designs. Then, there are several useful YouTube channels. I particularly liked System Design Fight Club, ByteByteGo (from the authors of System Design Interview), TRYEXCEPT, and Jordan has no life. I especially liked Jordan’s videos where he explained technologies or designed reference systems. A learning hack that worked for me was getting YouTube Premium, which allows for downloads and background play, and then listening to these videos while going for a walk. In conjunction with the more rigorous DDIA, this helped to solidify concepts and understand the big picture that sometimes is lost when working to understand technical details written on a page. When I was interviewing with a particular company, I was browsing their technical blogs and press releases to gather information about recent projects. With reading these resources and then looking for example System Design Interviews on YouTube in the same or an adjacent domain, I had a pretty decent hit rate of about 50% of having prepared a similar system design question to the one I got just the other day. Nonetheless, sometimes I got completely different system design questions, such as designing a Snapchat clone. As with the LeetCode interviews, I did a couple of mock interviews with friends. We used excalidraw, a website to draw boxes and put text, which is often used in real system design interviews as well. While I’ve experimented with voice AI to prepare these interviews, I found it too sycophantic to be useful beyond the practice of talking out loud. Culture fit The culture fit interview usually occurred after a few rounds. These rounds are designed to understand you as a person, what drives you, and if that matches the company. Questions can be of two types: 1) General behavioral questions (how one behaved in conflict situations or when things went south) and 2) company culture-specific questions (learn about them in the companies “About” page). To not blank in interviews, I spent some time to recall past behaviours beforehand.. I’ve prepared these stories in writing to avoid only remembering the perfect anecdote in the shower the next day. To this end, I found the STAR framework helpful. Situation: Where were you working, what was the team constellation, and what was the current goal? Task: What was your specific task, and why was it difficult? Action: What did you do to accomplish your task, overcome the difficulty, and contribute to achieving the team goal? Result: What was the final result of your efforts? I used STAR when putting the story into writing and mapping the different company values. I’ve also followed the STAR framework when telling the story in the interview to make sure I did not forget anything in forming a coherent narrative. Once again, I did practice culture fit interviews with friends and voice AI. Quiz Interview Knowledge, Quiz, or Fundamentals interviews are designed to map and find the edges of your expertise in a relevant subject area. They are harder to specifically prepare for than System Design or LeetCode interviews because they are less formulaic. In a way, they are designed to gauge the knowledge and experience acquired over a career and can’t be prepared with cramming the night before. I did, however, try to strategically refresh what I thought may be relevant based on the job description by skimming through books or lecture notes and listening to podcasts and YouTube videos. The Interviewers usually had prepared a couple of questions in advance. Sometimes they wanted answers to all of them; other times, they were just initial pointers that we used to riff on and have an interesting technical discussion without knowing where it would lead us. Generally, these interviews are purposefully pretty broad. I’ve encountered questions similar to these (made up) examples: How would you implement a set in your fork of a Python interpreter implementation, and what is the role of a hash function? How can you get error bars on the output of an LLM for a specific checkpoint, and how do you interpret their size? What is overfitting, what is double descent, and are modern deep learning models overparametrized? I think, the best preparation is to know the stuff on your CV and have enough knowledge on everything listed in the job description to say a couple of intelligent sentences about it. Since interviewers want to find the edge of your knowledge, it’s usually fine to say “I don’t know”. Whenever I wasn’t completely sure, I was also prefacing it with something along the lines of “I haven’t had practical exposure to distributed training until now, so my knowledge is theoretical. But you have data, model, and tensor parallelism …”. Hiring Manager / CTO Interview If I didn’t meet the hiring manager or CTO in an initial screen, I usually had a separate interview at the end of the process. When a company commits time to senior people, they are seriously considering hiring you. Since they have a picture of an applicant’s technical ability and culture fit at that point, the interview is much less rigorous. In essence, it’s a nice chat where the hiring manager or CTO tries to sell the role. Additionally, it’s a space to ask specific questions on how the team works together, what a first project may be, and what one would need to achieve to be deemed a successful hire. While these interviews seemed somewhat lower stakes since I had already cleared the technical bar, senior staff can definitely fail one if they think the vibe is off. I tried to be nice, excited, and had some questions about the company role and the personal motivation of my new superior. I’ve also used these interviews to gather insights about the company strategy and how my role and responsibilities might evolve a year or so in the future. Reference Check I’ve encountered reference checks usually as the last step before the contract, though some companies ask for them before moving into the first stages. This serves to cross-check CV claims and tests whether one is able to build and maintain relationships at school or previous work to get people to vouch for their name. I was asked to provide the name, contact details, relation, and job title of a couple (usually two) former peers so the company could reach out to them. I did ask my references before putting them down. Of course, because it’s etiquette, but also because I wanted to avoid my former manager being on a sabbatical, hiking through the Amazon without cellular reception, and not answering any inquiries about my previous performance. I think it’s best to put down people who worked closely with me and are thus familiar with my working style and the output quality. Bonus points if it is your manager or someone more senior, but a close relationship is definitely more important than seniority. The Mindgame On the one hand, changing jobs is great. It’s a period full of possibilities and leverage. I was in charge of shaping my future with a lot more negotiation power and ability to walk away than when I had been employed. This is what I tried to remind myself of when things got tough. It got tough. The process is taxing because it also includes a lot of rejection, uncertainty, inability to make long-term plans because I didn’t even know in which country I would end up, and, of course, living off savings and unemployment insurance. The worst part was that I was becoming aware of the stigma of being unemployed, which, as time progressed, made it increasingly harder not to simply accept a role that felt like too big a compromise. Then there is the endless wait for results, callbacks, or rejections. It’s nerve-racking, and I could do nothing to speed up the process. I also needed a lot of volitional energy and agency to navigate the constant friction between competing responsibilities. Should I rather fill the funnel with a couple of new applications, prepare the next rounds, or spend time with a strategic portfolio project to learn a new technology? While start-ups move fast, I found that competitive jobs at established companies or scale-ups take significant time. For me, that was around 2-3 months. Then it takes 2 weeks of back and forth to negotiate the contract and a couple more weeks to make the switch. So even if everything goes smoothly (and that is an if you cannot count on), a full-time job search is at least 4 months of a transitional state. Conclusion There you have it: my experiences and lessons of 18 months of job seeking. In essence, tactics boil down to two things: 1) Try to get an information advantage, and 2) act on this information to be prepared when it matters. This preparation can consist of strategic high-effort projects or tactical quick-win initiatives. I hope that this blog post gave you some information on what you are in for and how to best prepare. Outside of tactics, it’s strategy. These are things that take time and cannot be faked. Learn rare and valuable skills, build craft, and don’t forget to collect proof points of your abilities (technical artifacts, business outcomes, job titles, organisation membership) so others can easily gauge your level. Ideally, choose something you enjoy doing. It’s much easier to spend unreasonable amounts of time on getting better at something if you enjoy doing it. Build a network of peers and friends who know you, vouch for you, and send opportunities your way. These things are now what I will do at Mistral. Do good work, learn the codebase and new technologies, own parts of the product, grow more senior, make a couple of friends, and make the lives of my colleagues easier. Godspeed to all of us!

sentences.zh: 我发现 jobsearch.dev 是一个有用的资源，可以帮助您完成并提出这些标准（并且通常可以进入正确的应用程序空间）。

blocks.html_en: The Application Playbook

sentences.en: The Application Playbook
sentences.zh: 应用手册

blocks.html_en: With a goal defined, it’s time to get the ball rolling.

sentences.en: With a goal defined, it’s time to get the ball rolling.
sentences.zh: 确定了目标后，就该开始行动了。

blocks.html_en: I was introduced to this playbook right at the beginning of my journey by a friend working at a large Silicon Valley company, and promptly proceeded not to follow it for about a year. But when I finally did apply it, starting May 2025, with a polished portfolio and extensive LeetCode muscle memory, the results spoke for themselves.

sentences.en: I was introduced to this playbook right at the beginning of my journey by a friend working at a large Silicon Valley company, and promptly proceeded not to follow it for about a year.
sentences.zh: 在我的旅程开始时，一位在硅谷一家大公司工作的朋友向我介绍了这本手册，但很快我就开始在大约一年的时间里不再遵循它。

sentences.en: But when I finally did apply it, starting May 2025, with a polished portfolio and extensive LeetCode muscle memory, the results spoke for themselves.
sentences.zh: 但当我最终从 2025 年 5 月开始应用它时，凭借完善的投资组合和广泛的 LeetCode 肌肉记忆，结果不言而喻。

blocks.html_en: I used my predefined goal to compile a long list of positions and companies of interest. For my top choices, I tried to get in touch with people working there (or followed up with people I got to know in my exploration phase). The goal was to gather insider information on the application processes or sometimes even a referral.

sentences.en: I used my predefined goal to compile a long list of positions and companies of interest.
sentences.zh: 我根据预先设定的目标编制了一长串感兴趣的职位和公司名单。

sentences.en: For my top choices, I tried to get in touch with people working there (or followed up with people I got to know in my exploration phase).
sentences.zh: 对于我的最佳选择，我尝试与在那里工作的人取得联系（或跟踪我在探索阶段认识的人）。

sentences.en: The goal was to gather insider information on the application processes or sometimes even a referral.
sentences.zh: 目的是收集有关申请流程的内部信息，有时甚至是推荐信息。

blocks.html_en: This worked best with network contacts, but I had some luck with cold outreach on Twitter or LinkedIn. For cold outreach, I was writing something along the lines of: “I’m Max and really excited about xyz and strongly considering applying to role abc. Is there anything you can share to help me make the best possible application … ”

sentences.en: This worked best with network contacts, but I had some luck with cold outreach on Twitter or LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 这对于网络联系人效果最好，但我在 Twitter 或 LinkedIn 上的冷接触方面运气不错。

sentences.en: For cold outreach, I was writing something along the lines of: “I’m Max and really excited about xyz and strongly considering applying to role abc.
sentences.zh: 对于冷外展，我写了一些大致如下的内容：“我是 Max，对 xyz 感到非常兴奋，并强烈考虑申请 abc 角色。

sentences.en: Is there anything you can share to help me make the best possible application … ”
sentences.zh: 您有什么可以分享的，以帮助我做出最好的申请……”

blocks.html_en: I didn’t apply to all companies right away and instead proceeded in batches. Each batch contained one of my (referred) top choices as well as other companies I was less excited about, but would still consider working at.

sentences.en: I didn’t apply to all companies right away and instead proceeded in batches.
sentences.zh: 我并没有立即向所有公司申请，而是分批进行。

sentences.en: Each batch contained one of my (referred) top choices as well as other companies I was less excited about, but would still consider working at.
sentences.zh: 每一批都包含我（推荐的）最佳选择之一以及我不太感兴趣但仍会考虑工作的其他公司。

blocks.html_en: Proceeding through parallel processes in lockstep made coordination a lot easier. More importantly, I could schedule the lower-stakes interviews before the ones with my top choice. This way, you get some routine and do all the dumb first-time mistakes in a setting where the damage is reasonable.

sentences.en: Proceeding through parallel processes in lockstep made coordination a lot easier.
sentences.zh: 步调一致地进行并行流程使协调变得更加容易。

sentences.en: More importantly, I could schedule the lower-stakes interviews before the ones with my top choice.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，我可以在我的首选面试之前安排风险较低的面试。

sentences.en: This way, you get some routine and do all the dumb first-time mistakes in a setting where the damage is reasonable.
sentences.zh: 这样，你就可以得到一些常规，并在损害合理的情况下犯所有愚蠢的第一次错误。

blocks.html_en: I did not apply to companies where I was sure I wouldn’t want to work. There needs to be some stake in the process, and I don’t want to waste their time. While interviewing, some of these second-choice companies became first-choice ones throughout the process.

sentences.en: I did not apply to companies where I was sure I wouldn’t want to work.
sentences.zh: 我没有申请那些我确信自己不想工作的公司。

sentences.en: There needs to be some stake in the process, and I don’t want to waste their time.
sentences.zh: 这个过程中需要有一些利益，我不想浪费他们的时间。

sentences.en: While interviewing, some of these second-choice companies became first-choice ones throughout the process.
sentences.zh: 在面试过程中，一些第二选择的公司在整个过程中成为了第一选择。

blocks.html_en: For each batch, it was the goal to make it to the offer stage with multiple companies at the same time. Concrete offers gave a lot of signal to me. Which feels better and why? Additionally, multiple offers provide leverage in negotiations.

sentences.en: For each batch, it was the goal to make it to the offer stage with multiple companies at the same time.
sentences.zh: 对于每批产品，目标是同时与多家公司一起进入报价阶段。

sentences.en: Concrete offers gave a lot of signal to me.
sentences.zh: 具体的报价给了我很多信号。

sentences.en: Which feels better and why?
sentences.zh: 哪个感觉更好，为什么？

sentences.en: Additionally, multiple offers provide leverage in negotiations.
sentences.zh: 此外，多重报价可以在谈判中提供筹码。

blocks.html_en: Is there anything a company can do to make its package more attractive? Team assignment, signing bonus, remote work? I knew an ask was reasonable because I was offered the same by another place.

sentences.en: Is there anything a company can do to make its package more attractive?
sentences.zh: 公司可以做些什么来使其包装更具吸引力吗？

sentences.en: Team assignment, signing bonus, remote work?
sentences.zh: 团队分配、签约奖金、远程工作？

sentences.en: I knew an ask was reasonable because I was offered the same by another place.
sentences.zh: 我知道这个要求是合理的，因为另一个地方也向我提供了同样的要求。

blocks.html_en: The reason that I was having only one of my top choices in a batch is that I did feel some obligation to the referee. If I made it to an offer stage and the offer was competitive, I should take it.

sentences.en: The reason that I was having only one of my top choices in a batch is that I did feel some obligation to the referee.
sentences.zh: 我在一批中只有一个最佳选择的原因是我确实对裁判感到有一些义务。

sentences.en: If I made it to an offer stage and the offer was competitive, I should take it.
sentences.zh: 如果我进入了录用阶段并且该录用具有竞争力，我应该接受。

blocks.html_en: For the others, I wrote them after I had accepted my offer, thanked them for their advice that made getting this role possible, and promised to pay it forward (of which writing this blog post is a part).

sentences.en: For the others, I wrote them after I had accepted my offer, thanked them for their advice that made getting this role possible, and promised to pay it forward (of which writing this blog post is a part).
sentences.zh: 对于其他人，我在接受我的邀请后写了他们，感谢他们的建议，使我能够获得这个职位，并承诺将其转发（写这篇博客文章是其中的一部分）。

blocks.html_en: To reiterate, the essence of the playbook is:

sentences.en: To reiterate, the essence of the playbook is:
sentences.zh: 重申一下，该剧本的本质是：

blocks.html_en: 1) Batch your applications so you can use lower-stakes ones at training grounds

sentences.en: 1) Batch your applications so you can use lower-stakes ones at training grounds
sentences.zh: 1) 批量申请，以便您可以在训练场使用风险较低的申请

blocks.html_en: 2) Use your network to get referrals and insights into the interview process

sentences.en: 2) Use your network to get referrals and insights into the interview process
sentences.zh: 2）利用你的人际网络获得面试过程的推荐和见解

blocks.html_en: 3) Be mindful of your referee’s time and do your best to land the role they are referring you for

sentences.en: 3) Be mindful of your referee’s time and do your best to land the role they are referring you for
sentences.zh: 3) 注意推荐人的时间，并尽最大努力获得他们推荐给你的职位

blocks.html_en: Networks

sentences.en: Networks
sentences.zh: 网络

blocks.html_en: I’ve touched upon the importance of a professional network in the last section when talking about referrals and information about a company and its recruiting process.

sentences.en: I’ve touched upon the importance of a professional network in the last section when talking about referrals and information about a company and its recruiting process.
sentences.zh: 在上一节谈论有关公司及其招聘流程的推荐和信息时，我谈到了专业网络的重要性。

blocks.html_en: While friends in high places are surely useful, the main power of networks lies in the strength of weak ties. One generally has more acquaintances than close friends, and they know people far outside one’s own social circles.

sentences.en: While friends in high places are surely useful, the main power of networks lies in the strength of weak ties.
sentences.zh: 虽然身居高位的朋友固然有用，但网络的主要力量在于弱关系的力量。

sentences.en: One generally has more acquaintances than close friends, and they know people far outside one’s own social circles.
sentences.zh: 熟人一般多于密友，而且认识的人远远超出自己的社交圈子。

blocks.html_en: I still call these “acquaintances” friends, because to me, that is what they are. Personally, any “Networking” worked better when I took it as meeting interesting people, being helpful, and making friends, rather than making connections to my benefit. It also feels far less cringe. Either way, getting a warm introduction from a friend is a lot more powerful than cold outreach to a stranger.

sentences.en: I still call these “acquaintances” friends, because to me, that is what they are.
sentences.zh: 我仍然称这些“熟人”为朋友，因为对我来说，他们就是这样。

sentences.en: Personally, any “Networking” worked better when I took it as meeting interesting people, being helpful, and making friends, rather than making connections to my benefit.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，当我将任何“社交网络”视为结识有趣的人、乐于助人、结交朋友，而不是为了我的利益而建立联系时，它都会更有效。

sentences.en: It also feels far less cringe.
sentences.zh: 它也让人感觉不那么畏缩。

sentences.en: Either way, getting a warm introduction from a friend is a lot more powerful than cold outreach to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，从朋友那里得到热情的介绍比向陌生人冷淡的接触要有效得多。

blocks.html_en: I found LinkedIn a useful tool to figure out who knows who. But even more powerful than online stalking was talking to friends about my goals. Friends generally want to help, but to be useful, they need to know what you want to achieve.

sentences.en: I found LinkedIn a useful tool to figure out who knows who.
sentences.zh: 我发现 LinkedIn 是一个有用的工具，可以帮助我们了解谁认识谁。

sentences.en: But even more powerful than online stalking was talking to friends about my goals.
sentences.zh: 但比网上跟踪更强大的是与朋友谈论我的目标。

sentences.en: Friends generally want to help, but to be useful, they need to know what you want to achieve.
sentences.zh: 朋友通常都想提供帮助，但要想有用，他们需要知道你想要实现什么目标。

blocks.html_en: While using your network is tactical, building friendships can be strategic.

sentences.en: While using your network is tactical, building friendships can be strategic.
sentences.zh: 虽然使用网络是战术性的，但建立友谊可以是战略性的。

blocks.html_en: Online, I did so on Twitter/X. It is the only social media where I, through shared interests and banter in the comments, managed to build new relationships. Of course, there is a difference between a Twitter friend and someone you know for some time in real life, but I’ve got to know some mutual connections well enough that I felt comfortable asking for advice or help.

sentences.en: Online, I did so on Twitter/X.
sentences.zh: 在网上，我在 Twitter/X 上这样做了。

sentences.en: It is the only social media where I, through shared interests and banter in the comments, managed to build new relationships.
sentences.zh: 这是我通过共同兴趣和评论中的玩笑成功建立新关系的唯一社交媒体。

sentences.en: Of course, there is a difference between a Twitter friend and someone you know for some time in real life, but I’ve got to know some mutual connections well enough that I felt comfortable asking for advice or help.
sentences.zh: 当然，推特上的朋友和你在现实生活中认识一段时间的人之间是有区别的，但我必须足够了解一些相互关系，这样我才能放心地寻求建议或帮助。

blocks.html_en: Offline, it’s about going where people with similar interests go. That can be clubs, meetups, fairs, but also bootcamps, schools, or any other cohort-based programs. The latter are particularly effective, because people attending are more committed and usually in a phase of their life where they are especially open to new friendships.

sentences.en: Offline, it’s about going where people with similar interests go.
sentences.zh: 线下，就是去有相似兴趣的人去的地方。

sentences.en: That can be clubs, meetups, fairs, but also bootcamps, schools, or any other cohort-based programs.
sentences.zh: 这可以是俱乐部、聚会、博览会，也可以是训练营、学校或任何其他基于群体的项目。

sentences.en: The latter are particularly effective, because people attending are more committed and usually in a phase of their life where they are especially open to new friendships.
sentences.zh: 后者特别有效，因为参加的人更加忠诚，而且通常处于他们对新友谊特别开放的人生阶段。

blocks.html_en: Online and offline, my formula for making friends in the same domain works is (1) doing interesting things, (2) talking about them, and (3) being open and interested.

sentences.en: Online and offline, my formula for making friends in the same domain works is (1) doing interesting things, (2) talking about them, and (3) being open and interested.
sentences.zh: 无论在线上还是线下，我在同一领域结交朋友的秘诀是（1）做有趣的事情，（2）谈论这些事情，以及（3）保持开放和兴趣。

blocks.html_en: Doing things: You need to be active. Build projects, go to events, listen to talks, learn, and build craft. The “interesting” part comes almost on its own. If you do stuff that interests you, likely there are others who are also interested in it. It’s also something to bond over with others once you meet them.

sentences.en: Doing things: You need to be active.
sentences.zh: 做事：你需要积极主动。

sentences.en: Build projects, go to events, listen to talks, learn, and build craft.
sentences.zh: 构建项目、参加活动、聆听演讲、学习和打造工艺。

sentences.en: The “interesting” part comes almost on its own.
sentences.zh: “有趣”的部分几乎是自动出现的。

sentences.en: If you do stuff that interests you, likely there are others who are also interested in it.
sentences.zh: 如果你做自己感兴趣的事情，很可能其他人也对此感兴趣。

sentences.en: It’s also something to bond over with others once you meet them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你见到其他人，这也是一种与他们建立联系的东西。

blocks.html_en: Talk: People can only find you interesting if they know what makes you interesting. So post about your projects, talk to your friends about them, or give a presentation at your local Maker Space.

sentences.en: Talk: People can only find you interesting if they know what makes you interesting.
sentences.zh: 谈话：人们只有知道你的有趣之处，才会发现你有趣。

sentences.en: So post about your projects, talk to your friends about them, or give a presentation at your local Maker Space.
sentences.zh: 因此，发布您的项目，与您的朋友谈论它们，或者在当地的创客空间进行演示。

blocks.html_en: Being open: When people reach out to you, be open to talk and help. Trust and friendships form with repeated interactions. Choose to care about what is important to others. Help them if you can.

sentences.en: Being open: When people reach out to you, be open to talk and help.
sentences.zh: 保持开放：当人们向您伸出援手时，请开放地交谈并提供帮助。

sentences.en: Trust and friendships form with repeated interactions.
sentences.zh: 信任和友谊是通过反复的互动而形成的。

sentences.en: Choose to care about what is important to others.
sentences.zh: 选择关心对他人来说重要的事情。

sentences.en: Help them if you can.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话帮助他们。

blocks.html_en: How did I follow my own advice?

sentences.en: How did I follow my own advice?
sentences.zh: 我是如何遵循自己的建议的？

blocks.html_en: On Twitter, I was posting (sometimes daily) updates on my learning ML, Haskell, Kubernetes, or Rust, building a Compiler, or the struggles of writing a paper. It served as some public accountability structure and got me in touch with people who were doing the same, and was also a proof of work when someone stumbled across my profile. Blog posts about writing a Compiler (coming soon), an Interpreter, or this one serve the same purpose.

sentences.en: On Twitter, I was posting (sometimes daily) updates on my learning ML, Haskell, Kubernetes, or Rust, building a Compiler, or the struggles of writing a paper.
sentences.zh: 在 Twitter 上，我发布（有时每天）关于我学习 ML、Haskell、Kubernetes 或 Rust、构建编译器或撰写论文的困难的更新。

sentences.en: It served as some public accountability structure and got me in touch with people who were doing the same, and was also a proof of work when someone stumbled across my profile.
sentences.zh: 它充当了一些公共问责结构，让我与做同样事情的人取得联系，当有人偶然发现我的个人资料时，它也是一个工作证明。

sentences.en: Blog posts about writing a Compiler (coming soon), an Interpreter, or this one serve the same purpose.
sentences.zh: 关于编写编译器（即将推出）、解释器或这个的博客文章具有相同的目的。

blocks.html_en: All these are artifacts that others may find interesting. Some reach out via DMs — I try to answer all of them.

sentences.en: All these are artifacts that others may find interesting.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是其他人可能会感兴趣的工件。

sentences.en: Some reach out via DMs — I try to answer all of them.
sentences.zh: 有些人通过私信联系我——我尝试回答所有的问题。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes it’s also me doing the first step. Of course, it helps that I enjoy creating these artifacts, which makes them authentic. It also makes it easier to stomach if something that I spent a lot of work on making doesn’t find any resonance. Creating the piece was already some reward.

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s also me doing the first step.
sentences.zh: 有时也是我迈出了第一步。

sentences.en: Of course, it helps that I enjoy creating these artifacts, which makes them authentic.
sentences.zh: 当然，我喜欢创造这些文物，这让它们变得真实，这对我很有帮助。

sentences.en: It also makes it easier to stomach if something that I spent a lot of work on making doesn’t find any resonance.
sentences.zh: 如果我花了很多功夫制作的东西没有找到任何共鸣，这也让我更容易接受。

sentences.en: Creating the piece was already some reward.
sentences.zh: 创作这件作品已经是一些奖励了。

blocks.html_en: If you want to read more about why and how to share your progress and why you should do so, even if they aren’t polished, I recommend Show your work by Austin Kleon. It’s more geared toward artists, but the lessons generalize.

sentences.en: If you want to read more about why and how to share your progress and why you should do so, even if they aren’t polished, I recommend Show your work by Austin Kleon.
sentences.zh: 如果您想了解更多有关为什么以及如何分享您的进度以及为什么应该这样做的信息，即使它们尚未完善，我建议您展示 Austin Kleon 的作品。

sentences.en: It’s more geared toward artists, but the lessons generalize.
sentences.zh: 它更适合艺术家，但教训具有普遍性。

blocks.html_en: Building Career Momentum

sentences.en: Building Career Momentum
sentences.zh: 建立职业动力

blocks.html_en: Personal hot take: when organisations hire, they want to bet on winners. Winners can be All-Stars or up-and-coming underdogs. Either way, it’s necessary to demonstrate that this particular job is the logical next step on an upward trajectory. The artifacts you create to learn, build career capital, and a network can serve to build momentum toward a particular role.

sentences.en: Personal hot take: when organisations hire, they want to bet on winners.
sentences.zh: 个人热门观点：当组织招聘时，他们希望押注于获胜者。

sentences.en: Winners can be All-Stars or up-and-coming underdogs.
sentences.zh: 获胜者可以是全明星，也可以是崭露头角的失败者。

sentences.en: Either way, it’s necessary to demonstrate that this particular job is the logical next step on an upward trajectory.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，有必要证明这份特殊的工作是上升轨迹上合乎逻辑的下一步。

sentences.en: The artifacts you create to learn, build career capital, and a network can serve to build momentum toward a particular role.
sentences.zh: 您为学习、建立职业资本和网络而创建的工件可以为特定角色建立动力。

blocks.html_en: I wanted my interviewer to think something along the lines of: “This applicant has a rigorous quantitative base from degree ABC, now they became so interested in field DEF that they built a highly relevant portfolio project / OSS contributions / … in their own time”.

sentences.en: I wanted my interviewer to think something along the lines of: “This applicant has a rigorous quantitative base from degree ABC, now they became so interested in field DEF that they built a highly relevant portfolio project / OSS contributions / …
sentences.zh: 我希望我的面试官能够这样思考：“这位申请人拥有 ABC 学位严格的定量基础，现在他们对 DEF 领域非常感兴趣，以至于他们建立了一个高度相关的投资组合项目/OSS 贡献/……

sentences.en: in their own time”.
sentences.zh: 在他们自己的时间”。

blocks.html_en: This effectively means building career capital, a concept introduced to me in Cal Newport’s So Good They can’t Ignore You; the building of rare and valuable skills as well as ways (projects, positions, certificates, attended institutions, …) that verify these achievements to the outside.

sentences.en: This effectively means building career capital, a concept introduced to me in Cal Newport’s So Good They can’t Ignore You; the building of rare and valuable skills as well as ways (projects, positions, certificates, attended institutions, …)
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着建立职业资本，这是我在加州纽波特的《So Good They can't Ignore You》中向我介绍的一个概念；培养稀有且有价值的技能和方法（项目、职位、证书、就读机构……）

sentences.en: that verify these achievements to the outside.
sentences.zh: 向外界验证这些成就。

blocks.html_en: Ideally, previous roles serve as sufficient capital to open the next door. If there are missing skills — something easy to identify by reading the job description — I went on to strategically select portfolio projects and open source contributions to close the gap.

sentences.en: Ideally, previous roles serve as sufficient capital to open the next door.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，以前的角色可以作为打开下一扇门的足够资本。

sentences.en: If there are missing skills — something easy to identify by reading the job description — I went on to strategically select portfolio projects and open source contributions to close the gap.
sentences.zh: 如果缺少技能（通过阅读职位描述很容易识别），我会继续战略性地选择投资组合项目和开源贡献来缩小差距。

blocks.html_en: If there isn’t a clear progression from previous roles to the desired ones, degrees, and to a lesser extent, unaccredited programs such as bootcamps, trainings, summer schools, certificates, and the like, provide pivot points or even a “CV reset”.

sentences.en: If there isn’t a clear progression from previous roles to the desired ones, degrees, and to a lesser extent, unaccredited programs such as bootcamps, trainings, summer schools, certificates, and the like, provide pivot points or even a “CV reset”.
sentences.zh: 如果从以前的角色到所需的角色、学位没有明显的进展，并且在较小程度上，未经认可的项目（例如训练营、培训、暑期学校、证书等）可以提供关键点，甚至是“简历重置”。

blocks.html_en: Since it’s hard to give generalizable advice, I will discuss a couple of projects that I did to build skills and relevant career capital.

sentences.en: Since it’s hard to give generalizable advice, I will discuss a couple of projects that I did to build skills and relevant career capital.
sentences.zh: 由于很难提供普遍的建议，我将讨论我为培养技能和相关职业资本所做的几个项目。

blocks.html_en: Missing Work with LLMs Many of the Labs want you to have experience working with LLMs. I’ve built theoretical knowledge by reading Natural Language Processing with Transformers and built a project on idiosyncratic style transfer of small language models inspired by the TinyStories dataset. To give the project a little more weight when talking about it and forcing it into completion, I signed up for a presentation at an AI Tinkerers event (also a great opportunity to make new friends). This gave me a repository I could add to my portfolio and the measurable success metric “presented to an audience of 100+“.

sentences.en: Missing Work with LLMs Many of the Labs want you to have experience working with LLMs.
sentences.zh: 缺少与法学硕士的合作 许多实验室希望您拥有与法学硕士合作的经验。

sentences.en: I’ve built theoretical knowledge by reading Natural Language Processing with Transformers and built a project on idiosyncratic style transfer of small language models inspired by the TinyStories dataset.
sentences.zh: 我通过阅读《使用 Transformers 进行自然语言处理》积累了理论知识，并在 TinyStories 数据集的启发下建立了一个关于小语言模型的特殊风格迁移的项目。

sentences.en: To give the project a little more weight when talking about it and forcing it into completion, I signed up for a presentation at an AI Tinkerers event (also a great opportunity to make new friends).
sentences.zh: 为了在谈论该项目并迫使其完成时给予该项目更多的重视，我报名参加了 AI Tinkerers 活动的演讲（也是结交新朋友的绝佳机会）。

sentences.en: This gave me a repository I could add to my portfolio and the measurable success metric “presented to an audience of 100+“.
sentences.zh: 这给了我一个可以添加到我的投资组合中的存储库，以及“向 100 多名观众展示”的可衡量的成功指标。

blocks.html_en: No CS Background I’m essentially a self-taught engineer and sometimes felt that people were doubting my theoretical and practical foundations, especially when it came to performance engineering. To this end, I decided to learn Rust, a performance-oriented systems-level language, and get it to a level where I could comfortably contribute to production codebases. I made this measurable by getting 15+ pull requests merged in Ruff and UV. Doing this as part of a three-month batch at Recurse Center gave me the freedom to focus on this full-time, as well as a complete entry on my CV to communicate the achievements.

sentences.en: No CS Background I’m essentially a self-taught engineer and sometimes felt that people were doubting my theoretical and practical foundations, especially when it came to performance engineering.
sentences.zh: 没有计算机科学背景我本质上是一名自学成才的工程师，有时觉得人们怀疑我的理论和实践基础，尤其是在性能工程方面。

sentences.en: To this end, I decided to learn Rust, a performance-oriented systems-level language, and get it to a level where I could comfortably contribute to production codebases.
sentences.zh: 为此，我决定学习 Rust，一种面向性能的系统级语言，并将其提升到可以轻松为生产代码库做出贡献的水平。

sentences.en: I made this measurable by getting 15+ pull requests merged in Ruff and UV.
sentences.zh: 我通过在 Ruff 和 UV 中合并 15 个以上的拉取请求来实现这一点。

sentences.en: Doing this as part of a three-month batch at Recurse Center gave me the freedom to focus on this full-time, as well as a complete entry on my CV to communicate the achievements.
sentences.zh: 作为在递归中心为期三个月的批次的一部分，我可以自由地全职专注于这项工作，并在我的简历中完整地记录我的成就。

blocks.html_en: Missing Publications Publications are often listed as desired qualifications in ML Research positions. I didn’t have any. To address this, I got in touch with my thesis supervisor from four years ago and reworked my thesis into a publication we want to submit to a peer-reviewed journal. As of now, it isn’t published, but I added it as a work in progress on my CV (using the Recurse entry as both occurred roughly at the same time).

sentences.en: Missing Publications Publications are often listed as desired qualifications in ML Research positions.
sentences.zh: 缺少出版物 出版物通常被列为机器学习研究职位所需的资格。

sentences.en: I didn’t have any.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: To address this, I got in touch with my thesis supervisor from four years ago and reworked my thesis into a publication we want to submit to a peer-reviewed journal.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，我与四年前的论文导师取得了联系，并将我的论文修改为我们想要提交给同行评审期刊的出版物。

sentences.en: As of now, it isn’t published, but I added it as a work in progress on my CV (using the Recurse entry as both occurred roughly at the same time).
sentences.zh: 截至目前，它尚未发布，但我将其添加为我的简历中的一项正在进行的工作（使用递归条目，因为两者几乎同时发生）。

blocks.html_en: While job descriptions often gave special weight to venues like NeurIPS or ICML, I figured any peer-reviewed research would get me 80% there. I was also convinced that I already possessed the research chops companies want to proxy for by demanding publications. Thus, opting to extend my thesis research at the intersection of information theory and complex systems was a great effort-signal trade-off and essentially continuing work I had already done to a point where it gives signal to those reading my CV. This is especially true, given that my supervisor works for the AI Safety Institute of the German Aerospace Centre, which allows for some AI/ML namedropping. It had the additional benefit of working closely with my supervisor again, which gave him lots to talk about when I put him down as a reference.

sentences.en: While job descriptions often gave special weight to venues like NeurIPS or ICML, I figured any peer-reviewed research would get me 80% there.
sentences.zh: 虽然职位描述通常特别重视 NeurIPS 或 ICML 等场所，但我认为任何经过同行评审的研究都能让我获得 80% 的分数。

sentences.en: I was also convinced that I already possessed the research chops companies want to proxy for by demanding publications.
sentences.zh: 我还确信我已经具备了公司希望通过高要求出版物来获得的研究能力。

sentences.en: Thus, opting to extend my thesis research at the intersection of information theory and complex systems was a great effort-signal trade-off and essentially continuing work I had already done to a point where it gives signal to those reading my CV.
sentences.zh: 因此，选择在信息论和复杂系统的交叉点扩展我的论文研究是一个巨大的努力-信号权衡，本质上是继续我已经完成的工作，直到它向那些阅读我的简历的人发出信号。

sentences.en: This is especially true, given that my supervisor works for the AI Safety Institute of the German Aerospace Centre, which allows for some AI/ML namedropping.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我的主管在德国航空航天中心的人工智能安全研究所工作，这一点尤其正确，该研究所允许进行一些人工智能/机器学习的命名。

sentences.en: It had the additional benefit of working closely with my supervisor again, which gave him lots to talk about when I put him down as a reference.
sentences.zh: 它还有一个额外的好处，那就是再次与我的主管密切合作，当我把他作为推荐人时，这给了他很多可以谈论的话题。

blocks.html_en: Each of these was a considerable amount of work. In the end, there is no shortcut to building rare and valuable skills; otherwise, they wouldn’t be rare.

sentences.en: Each of these was a considerable amount of work.
sentences.zh: 每一项都是相当大量的工作。

sentences.en: In the end, there is no shortcut to building rare and valuable skills; otherwise, they wouldn’t be rare.
sentences.zh: 最后，培养稀有且有价值的技能没有捷径；不然的话，也不会稀有。

blocks.html_en: With limited time, it’s sensible to select projects that tick several boxes with a single measure. I used my research to dabble with system level programming in C++ (before pivoting to Rust), RC served as a pivot point as well as giving me the time to dive deep into systems programming and open source work and the talk about my LLM project is evidence to my communication ability, serves as a “business outcome” and turns dabbling into something serious. This works best for projects where one already possesses the skills and only needs a way to communicate them.

sentences.en: With limited time, it’s sensible to select projects that tick several boxes with a single measure.
sentences.zh: 在时间有限的情况下，明智的做法是选择通过单一措施满足多个条件的项目。

sentences.en: I used my research to dabble with system level programming in C++ (before pivoting to Rust), RC served as a pivot point as well as giving me the time to dive deep into systems programming and open source work and the talk about my LLM project is evidence to my communication ability, serves as a “business outcome” and turns dabbling into something serious.
sentences.zh: 我利用我的研究涉足 C++ 系统级编程（在转向 Rust 之前），RC 作为一个支点，让我有时间深入研究系统编程和开源工作，关于我的 LLM 项目的讨论证明了我的沟通能力，作为“业务成果”，并将涉足变成了严肃的事情。

sentences.en: This works best for projects where one already possesses the skills and only needs a way to communicate them.
sentences.zh: 这最适合那些已经拥有技能并且只需要一种沟通方式的项目。

blocks.html_en: Long term, however, fewer high-quality projects that take considerable effort to complete are almost always better than many shallow ones. Building career momentum is not about gaming the system; it’s about doing the work and learning the skills.

sentences.en: Long term, however, fewer high-quality projects that take considerable effort to complete are almost always better than many shallow ones.
sentences.zh: 然而，从长远来看，少数需要付出大量努力才能完成的高质量项目几乎总是比许多肤浅的项目要好。

sentences.en: Building career momentum is not about gaming the system; it’s about doing the work and learning the skills.
sentences.zh: 建立职业动力并不是要玩弄制度，而是要玩弄制度。这是关于做工作和学习技能。

blocks.html_en: Application Process Touch Points

sentences.en: Application Process Touch Points
sentences.zh: 申请流程接触点

blocks.html_en: Once I had built a network, strategic career capital, and enough portfolio projects that I was getting my foot in the door for interviews, it got tactical again.

sentences.en: Once I had built a network, strategic career capital, and enough portfolio projects that I was getting my foot in the door for interviews, it got tactical again.
sentences.zh: 一旦我建立了一个网络、战略职业资本和足够的投资组合项目，我就可以踏入面试的大门，它再次变得战术性的。

blocks.html_en: What follows is a description of the different types of interviews I encountered in application processes and how I prepared for them. Remember the application playbook section for tips on real-life interview practice.

sentences.en: What follows is a description of the different types of interviews I encountered in application processes and how I prepared for them.
sentences.zh: 以下是我在申请过程中遇到的不同类型的面试以及我如何准备面试的描述。

sentences.en: Remember the application playbook section for tips on real-life interview practice.
sentences.zh: 请记住申请手册部分，了解现实生活中面试练习的技巧。

blocks.html_en: But there were some things I did in preparation for every interview:

sentences.en: But there were some things I did in preparation for every interview:
sentences.zh: 但在准备每次面试时我都做了一些事情：

blocks.html_en: • If I knew the Interviewer, I was looking at their LinkedIn, GitHub, Twitter, blog, etc. This helped me to set focus points in preparation and come up with questions, etc., in the chit-chat that comes before or after the meat of the interview.

sentences.en: If I knew the Interviewer, I was looking at their LinkedIn, GitHub, Twitter, blog, etc. This helped me to set focus points in preparation and come up with questions, etc., in the chit-chat that comes before or after the meat of the interview.
sentences.zh: 如果我认识面试官，我就会查看他们的 LinkedIn、GitHub、Twitter、博客等。这有助于我在准备过程中设定重点，并在面试的重点之前或之后的闲聊中提出问题等。

blocks.html_en: • I’ve read up on recent releases and products of the company or team I was applying to.

sentences.en: I’ve read up on recent releases and products of the company or team I was applying to.
sentences.zh: 我已经阅读了我所申请的公司或团队的最新版本和产品。

blocks.html_en: • I knew the company values (at least roughly) and why I wanted to work for this organisation specifically.

sentences.en: I knew the company values (at least roughly) and why I wanted to work for this organisation specifically.
sentences.zh: 我了解公司的价值观（至少大致了解）以及为什么我想专门为这个组织工作。

blocks.html_en: • I knew the specific position, what I hoped to get out of it, and why my previous experience would make me a perfect candidate.

sentences.en: I knew the specific position, what I hoped to get out of it, and why my previous experience would make me a perfect candidate.
sentences.zh: 我知道具体的职位，我希望从中得到什么，以及为什么我以前的经验会让我成为一个完美的候选人。

blocks.html_en: • I had a couple of questions prepared, which I could ask at the end of the interview if the interviewer gave me the space to do so (they almost always did).

sentences.en: I had a couple of questions prepared, which I could ask at the end of the interview if the interviewer gave me the space to do so (they almost always did).
sentences.zh: 我准备了几个问题，如果面试官给我空间，我可以在面试结束时问这些问题（他们几乎总是这样做）。

blocks.html_en: In general, these can be summarised as me trying to be prepared and having done my homework.

sentences.en: In general, these can be summarised as me trying to be prepared and having done my homework.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这些可以概括为我正在努力做好准备并做好功课。

blocks.html_en: All my interviews were remote video calls. That’s why I don’t have any experience preparing for on-sites.

sentences.en: All my interviews were remote video calls.
sentences.zh: 我所有的采访都是远程视频通话。

sentences.en: That’s why I don’t have any experience preparing for on-sites.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我没有任何现场准备的经验。

blocks.html_en: Referrals

sentences.en: Referrals
sentences.zh: 推荐人

blocks.html_en: I’ve already touched upon this in the networking section above. For all my favourite positions, I was trying to get referrals via friends, friends-of-friends, or people I had interacted with for some time on Twitter or LinkedIn.

sentences.en: I’ve already touched upon this in the networking section above.
sentences.zh: 我已经在上面的网络部分谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: For all my favourite positions, I was trying to get referrals via friends, friends-of-friends, or people I had interacted with for some time on Twitter or LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 对于所有我最喜欢的职位，我都试图通过朋友、朋友的朋友或我在 Twitter 或 LinkedIn 上互动过一段时间的人获得推荐。

blocks.html_en: I asked warm leads for referrals right away. Those whom I only knew online, I tried to get to know in a call or, even better, a physical meeting, asking for general advice on careers or insights on the role and company. I then only asked for a referral if the vibes permitted (sometimes I was even offered one). Since referees often get a bonus if I land the job, there are some aligned incentives.

sentences.en: I asked warm leads for referrals right away.
sentences.zh: 我立即向热情的线索寻求推荐。

sentences.en: Those whom I only knew online, I tried to get to know in a call or, even better, a physical meeting, asking for general advice on careers or insights on the role and company.
sentences.zh: 对于那些我只在网上认识的人，我试图通过电话或更好的面对面会议来了解，询问有关职业的一般建议或对职位和公司的见解。

sentences.en: I then only asked for a referral if the vibes permitted (sometimes I was even offered one).
sentences.zh: 然后，如果氛围允许，我只会要求推荐（有时甚至有人向我提供推荐）。

sentences.en: Since referees often get a bonus if I land the job, there are some aligned incentives.
sentences.zh: 由于如果我找到工作，推荐人通常会获得奖金，因此有一些一致的激励措施。

blocks.html_en: Still, I only got referrals to roles I was really excited about. I think it’s okay to decline an offer in favour of another. But declining an offer without an alternative makes a referee look bad. I didn’t want to risk that with roles I wasn’t completely sure about.

sentences.en: Still, I only got referrals to roles I was really excited about.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我只得到了我真正感兴趣的角色的推荐。

sentences.en: I think it’s okay to decline an offer in favour of another.
sentences.zh: 我认为拒绝一个提议并转而接受另一个提议是可以的。

sentences.en: But declining an offer without an alternative makes a referee look bad.
sentences.zh: 但在没有其他选择的情况下拒绝报价会让裁判看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: I didn’t want to risk that with roles I wasn’t completely sure about.
sentences.zh: 我不想冒这样的风险去扮演我不完全确定的角色。

blocks.html_en: CV

The first thing to kick off the application process was submitting my CV. I don’t think a CV needs to be a comprehensive history of employment. Instead, it should highlight the aspects of my professional experience relevant to the roles that I am gunning for.

sentences.en: The first thing to kick off the application process was submitting my CV.
sentences.zh: 开始申请流程的第一件事就是提交我的简历。

sentences.en: I don’t think a CV needs to be a comprehensive history of employment.
sentences.zh: 我认为简历不需要包含全面的工作经历。

sentences.en: Instead, it should highlight the aspects of my professional experience relevant to the roles that I am gunning for.
sentences.zh: 相反，它应该突出我的专业经验与我所追求的角色相关的方面。

blocks.html_en: In terms of layout, I used different typefaces, font sizes, and colors to make it easy to read while keeping everything else as conservative as possible; one column, no fancy design elements beyond blue colored links.

sentences.en: In terms of layout, I used different typefaces, font sizes, and colors to make it easy to read while keeping everything else as conservative as possible; one column, no fancy design elements beyond blue colored links.
sentences.zh: 在布局方面，我使用了不同的字体、字体大小和颜色，以使其易于阅读，同时保持其他一切尽可能保守；一栏，除了蓝色链接之外没有任何花哨的设计元素。

blocks.html_en: Basically, I was imagining the hiring manager reading my CV on their phone, on the way to the office kitchen, semi-engaged in a discussion with colleagues. They have only some glances at the screen to get the gist: I’m an ML Engineer, my previous positions, and relevant projects.

sentences.en: Basically, I was imagining the hiring manager reading my CV on their phone, on the way to the office kitchen, semi-engaged in a discussion with colleagues.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我想象招聘经理在去办公室厨房的路上用手机阅读我的简历，半参与与同事的讨论。

sentences.en: They have only some glances at the screen to get the gist: I’m an ML Engineer, my previous positions, and relevant projects.
sentences.zh: 他们只需扫一眼屏幕即可了解要点：我是一名机器学习工程师、我以前的职位以及相关项目。

blocks.html_en: As such, I made it a top priority to keep my CV to a single one-column page. If they weren’t scrolling, everything that is on the second page is lost anyway. The purpose of the single column was to be more parsable to automated applicant tracking systems.

sentences.en: As such, I made it a top priority to keep my CV to a single one-column page.
sentences.zh: 因此，我将简历保留在单栏页面上作为首要任务。

sentences.en: If they weren’t scrolling, everything that is on the second page is lost anyway.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不滚动，第二页上的所有内容都会丢失。

sentences.en: The purpose of the single column was to be more parsable to automated applicant tracking systems.
sentences.zh: 单列的目的是为了更容易被自动申请人跟踪系统解析。

blocks.html_en: I have four sections on my CV: 1) Work Experience, 2) Portfolio, 3) Education, and 4) Skills. People fresh out of school may want to put education higher, as it is their main qualification.

sentences.en: I have four sections on my CV: 1) Work Experience, 2) Portfolio, 3) Education, and 4) Skills.
sentences.zh: 我的简历有四个部分：1) 工作经验，2) 作品集，3) 教育背景，4) 技能。

sentences.en: People fresh out of school may want to put education higher, as it is their main qualification.
sentences.zh: 刚从学校毕业的人可能希望接受更高的教育，因为这是他们的主要资格。

blocks.html_en: Each entry contained a small description of my tasks, their successful outcomes, and the technologies used, set in a smaller font. I want the hiring manager to read the text block of the most relevant experience. They should get excited about me instead of being bored by uninteresting details elsewhere.

sentences.en: Each entry contained a small description of my tasks, their successful outcomes, and the technologies used, set in a smaller font.
sentences.zh: 每个条目都包含对我的任务、其成功结果以及所使用的技术的简短描述，并以较小的字体设置。

sentences.en: I want the hiring manager to read the text block of the most relevant experience.
sentences.zh: 我希望招聘经理阅读最相关经验的文本块。

sentences.en: They should get excited about me instead of being bored by uninteresting details elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 他们应该对我感到兴奋，而不是对其他地方无趣的细节感到无聊。

blocks.html_en: Whenever available, I added metrics to add credibility and quantify my impact. The one exception is the summary at the top of the CV. I wanted to keep it succinct. This makes it especially important that all claims in the summary are supported by several of the other entries in my CV.

sentences.en: Whenever available, I added metrics to add credibility and quantify my impact.
sentences.zh: 只要有可能，我都会添加指标来增加可信度并量化我的影响。

sentences.en: The one exception is the summary at the top of the CV.
sentences.zh: 唯一的例外是简历顶部的摘要。

sentences.en: I wanted to keep it succinct.
sentences.zh: 我想保持简洁。

sentences.en: This makes it especially important that all claims in the summary are supported by several of the other entries in my CV.
sentences.zh: 因此，摘要中的所有主张都得到我简历中其他几个条目的支持就显得尤为重要。

blocks.html_en: Besides metrics, I’ve added hyperlinks to GitHub code or other public assets. If something is interesting, people can check it out. The fact that the links are blue also allows me to highlight things I really want the reader to see. As eyes quickly scan the document, they will likely register the link text.

sentences.en: Besides metrics, I’ve added hyperlinks to GitHub code or other public assets.
sentences.zh: 除了指标之外，我还添加了指向 GitHub 代码或其他公共资产的超链接。

sentences.en: If something is interesting, people can check it out.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么有趣的事情，人们可以查看。

sentences.en: The fact that the links are blue also allows me to highlight things I really want the reader to see.
sentences.zh: 事实上，链接是蓝色的，这也让我能够突出显示我真正希望读者看到的内容。

sentences.en: As eyes quickly scan the document, they will likely register the link text.

sentences.en: This introduction is something that, albeit in shorter form, repeats every interview, and I prepared and practiced this beforehand.

sentences.en: In the end, my introduction looked something like this:
sentences.zh: 最后，我的介绍是这样的：

sentences.en: “Hi, I’m Max, a Machine Learning engineer.
sentences.zh: “嗨，我是 Max，一名机器学习工程师。

sentences.en: You’ve probably read my CV, so I will just briefly summarise what makes me uniquely qualified for this role.

blocks.html_en: Depending on the company (and interviewer) vibe, I would also add a personal touch, such as hobbies and interests. Practicing the same sport as the interviewer made for easy sympathy points.

sentences.en: Depending on the company (and interviewer) vibe, I would also add a personal touch, such as hobbies and interests.

sentences.zh: 与采访者进行同样的运动很容易引起同情。

blocks.html_en: The initial screen then proceeded with follow-up questions on specific projects and business outcomes that I had listed on my CV. The best advice I can give is to know it thoroughly. This should be easy; it’s your life after all.

sentences.en: The initial screen then proceeded with follow-up questions on specific projects and business outcomes that I had listed on my CV.
sentences.zh: 然后，初始筛选继续针对我在简历中列出的特定项目和业务成果提出后续问题。

sentences.en: The best advice I can give is to know it thoroughly.
sentences.zh: 我能给出的最好建议就是彻底了解它。

sentences.en: This should be easy; it’s your life after all.
sentences.zh: 这应该很容易；毕竟这是你的生活。

blocks.html_en: Takehome

sentences.en: Takehome
sentences.zh: 带回家

blocks.html_en: Takehomes are programming challenges that I was tasked to work on asynchronously. I got them via email, usually with a deadline of a couple of days to a week in the future. Sometimes I was just judged on what I submitted; other times, there was a follow-up interview where we talked through my solution.

sentences.en: Takehomes are programming challenges that I was tasked to work on asynchronously.
sentences.zh: 我的收获是异步处理的编程挑战。

sentences.en: I got them via email, usually with a deadline of a couple of days to a week in the future.
sentences.zh: 我通过电子邮件收到它们，截止日期通常是未来几天到一周。

sentences.en: Sometimes I was just judged on what I submitted; other times, there was a follow-up interview where we talked through my solution.
sentences.zh: 有时我只是根据我提交的内容来评判;其他时候，我们会进行后续采访，讨论我的解决方案。

blocks.html_en: The contents of the takehomes are pretty idiosyncratic to the company in question. These are some of the takehomes I’ve encountered personally or seen with friends.

sentences.en: The contents of the takehomes are pretty idiosyncratic to the company in question.
sentences.zh: 总结的内容对于相关公司来说非常独特。

sentences.en: These are some of the takehomes I’ve encountered personally or seen with friends.
sentences.zh: 这些是我亲自遇到或与朋友一起看到的一些收获。

blocks.html_en: • You’re being supplied a specification and can submit code to run against a test suite

sentences.en: You’re being supplied a specification and can submit code to run against a test suite
sentences.zh: 您将获得一份规范，并且可以提交代码以针对测试套件运行

blocks.html_en: • You are giving a small ticket, access to their codebase, and should solve the issue (this interview step was compensated with ~500 USD)

sentences.en: You are giving a small ticket, access to their codebase, and should solve the issue (this interview step was compensated with ~500 USD)
sentences.zh: 您将获得一张小票，可以访问他们的代码库，并应该解决问题（此采访步骤的补偿约为 500 美元）

blocks.html_en: • I was given LLM training code, and the resulting model produced gibberish. I should identify 10 bugs in the code.

sentences.en: I was given LLM training code, and the resulting model produced gibberish.
sentences.zh: 我得到了 LLM 培训代码，但生成的模型产生了乱码。

sentences.en: I should identify 10 bugs in the code.
sentences.zh: 我应该找出代码中的 10 个错误。

blocks.html_en: For the most part, these takehomes had an expected time to spend on them. I always spent far more because the roles were important to me.

sentences.en: For the most part, these takehomes had an expected time to spend on them.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，这些带回家的东西都有预期的时间来花在它们上。

sentences.en: I always spent far more because the roles were important to me.
sentences.zh: 我总是花更多的钱，因为这些角色对我来说很重要。

blocks.html_en: I got my first takehomes while I was still working for my previous employer. Completing the tasks and having a crunch phase at work resulted in a pretty heavy week.

sentences.en: I got my first takehomes while I was still working for my previous employer.
sentences.zh: 当我还在为前雇主工作时，我得到了第一个收获。

sentences.en: Completing the tasks and having a crunch phase at work resulted in a pretty heavy week.
sentences.zh: 完成任务并在工作中度过一个关键阶段，这让我们度过了相当沉重的一周。

blocks.html_en: This experience was one of the major drivers for the decision to quit and then be able to commit full-time to searching for a new job. I don’t see how one can realistically do multiple of these challenges simultaneously in a sufficient quality for different applications while holding a job.

sentences.en: This experience was one of the major drivers for the decision to quit and then be able to commit full-time to searching for a new job.
sentences.zh: 这种经历是决定辞职然后能够全职寻找新工作的主要驱动力之一。

sentences.en: I don’t see how one can realistically do multiple of these challenges simultaneously in a sufficient quality for different applications while holding a job.
sentences.zh: 我不明白一个人如何能够在保住一份工作的同时，以足够的质量同时应对不同的应用程序中的多个挑战。

blocks.html_en: Online Assessment

sentences.en: Online Assessment
sentences.zh: 在线评估

blocks.html_en: Besides programming interviews and takehomes, I’ve also encountered online assessments. They are asynchronous, but have a time limit on the order of hours instead of days, as with the takehomes.

sentences.en: Besides programming interviews and takehomes, I’ve also encountered online assessments.
sentences.zh: 除了编程面试和总结之外，我还遇到过在线评估。

sentences.en: They are asynchronous, but have a time limit on the order of hours instead of days, as with the takehomes.
sentences.zh: 它们是异步的，但有几个小时的时间限制，而不是像回家一样的几天。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes they are proctored, which means that you have to film yourself and share a screen recording so that they can ensure it’s you taking the test and that you are not using prohibited aids.

sentences.en: Sometimes they are proctored, which means that you have to film yourself and share a screen recording so that they can ensure it’s you taking the test and that you are not using prohibited aids.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会受到监考，这意味着您必须拍摄自己并分享屏幕录像，以便他们可以确保是您在参加考试并且您没有使用违禁的辅助工具。

blocks.html_en: In essence, they are similar to programming interviews, just with automated tests and no interviewer present.

sentences.en: In essence, they are similar to programming interviews, just with automated tests and no interviewer present.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它们类似于编程面试，只是采用自动化测试并且没有面试官在场。

blocks.html_en: Programming Interview

sentences.en: Programming Interview
sentences.zh: 编程面试

blocks.html_en: Programming interviews are the core of the software and ML engineering interview process, and they have been part of every interview process I’ve encountered. They come in several different forms, which we discuss shortly.

sentences.en: Programming interviews are the core of the software and ML engineering interview process, and they have been part of every interview process I’ve encountered.
sentences.zh: 编程面试是软件和机器学习工程面试过程的核心，也是我遇到的每个面试过程的一部分。

sentences.en: They come in several different forms, which we discuss shortly.
sentences.zh: 它们有几种不同的形式，我们很快就会讨论。

blocks.html_en: But first, talk about general advice. They all serve a common goal: to evaluate how you think, break down a problem, think about edge cases, and work toward the solution of a programming problem.

sentences.en: But first, talk about general advice.
sentences.zh: 但首先，谈谈一般建议。

sentences.en: They all serve a common goal: to evaluate how you think, break down a problem, think about edge cases, and work toward the solution of a programming problem.
sentences.zh: 它们都有一个共同的目标：评估您的思维方式、分解问题、考虑边缘情况并努力解决编程问题。

blocks.html_en: In the process, companies want to see your communication and collaboration skills. To that end, it’s imperative that you talk out loud. I think it’s fine to read the exercise and think for a minute in silence, but after that, I was verbalizing my thought process to give the interviewer enough signal to judge my ability beyond a binary pass/fail of the task.

sentences.en: In the process, companies want to see your communication and collaboration skills.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，公司希望看到你的沟通和协作能力。

sentences.en: To that end, it’s imperative that you talk out loud.
sentences.zh: 为此，你必须大声说出来。

sentences.en: I think it’s fine to read the exercise and think for a minute in silence, but after that, I was verbalizing my thought process to give the interviewer enough signal to judge my ability beyond a binary pass/fail of the task.
sentences.zh: 我认为阅读练习并安静地思考一分钟是可以的，但在那之后，我会用语言表达我的思维过程，以便给面试官足够的信号来判断我的能力，而不仅仅是任务的二元通过/失败。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes, the Interviewers gave me hints or helped me to avoid exploring an impasse. Of course, it’s better to pass without any interventions, but it’s a lot better to get the code to work with help than not work at all. If I were stuck, I would try to explain where and why. Sometimes that was enough to figure out a solution myself, but it also presented a possibility for the interviewer to nudge me in the right direction.

sentences.en: Sometimes, the Interviewers gave me hints or helped me to avoid exploring an impasse.
sentences.zh: 有时，面试官会给我提示或帮助我避免陷入僵局。

sentences.en: Of course, it’s better to pass without any interventions, but it’s a lot better to get the code to work with help than not work at all.
sentences.zh: 当然，最好在没有任何干预的情况下通过，但在帮助下让代码工作比根本不工作要好得多。

sentences.en: If I were stuck, I would try to explain where and why.
sentences.zh: 如果我被困住了，我会尝试解释在哪里以及为什么。

sentences.en: Sometimes that was enough to figure out a solution myself, but it also presented a possibility for the interviewer to nudge me in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 有时这足以让我自己找出解决方案，但它也为面试官提供了将我推向正确方向的可能性。

blocks.html_en: Let’s now discuss the different kinds of programming interviews in more detail.

sentences.en: Let’s now discuss the different kinds of programming interviews in more detail.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们更详细地讨论不同类型的编程面试。

blocks.html_en: Leetcode Type Interview

sentences.en: Leetcode Type Interview
sentences.zh: Leetcode 类型面试

blocks.html_en: The most common coding interview questions are LeetCode or LeetCode-style questions that are adapted to the domain in which the company operates.

sentences.en: The most common coding interview questions are LeetCode or LeetCode-style questions that are adapted to the domain in which the company operates.
sentences.zh: 最常见的编码面试问题是 LeetCode 或 LeetCode 风格的问题，这些问题适用于公司运营的领域。

blocks.html_en: In all these interviews, I was asked to share my screen. Sometimes using my own editor, sometimes coding in Google Docs, but most often in a Coderpad online interpreter.

sentences.en: In all these interviews, I was asked to share my screen.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些采访中，我都被要求分享我的屏幕。

sentences.en: Sometimes using my own editor, sometimes coding in Google Docs, but most often in a Coderpad online interpreter.
sentences.zh: 有时使用我自己的编辑器，有时在 Google Docs 中编码，但最常见的是使用 Coderpad 在线解释器。

blocks.html_en: Whenever there was an interpreter, we ran my code against tests. If they failed, I used the test output for debugging. Generally, it helped to think through the problem first and get buy-in for a high-level pseudo-code solution written out in comments before writing out the actual code.

sentences.en: Whenever there was an interpreter, we ran my code against tests.
sentences.zh: 每当有解释器时，我们就会根据测试运行我的代码。

sentences.en: If they failed, I used the test output for debugging.
sentences.zh: 如果失败，我会使用测试输出进行调试。

sentences.en: Generally, it helped to think through the problem first and get buy-in for a high-level pseudo-code solution written out in comments before writing out the actual code.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，它有助于首先思考问题，并在编写实际代码之前获得在注释中写出的高级伪代码解决方案的支持。

blocks.html_en: If I could choose the language for the interview, I would choose Python. Partly because it’s a language I’m pretty well versed in, but also because I didn’t want to deal with memory issues in an algorithmic interview.

sentences.en: If I could choose the language for the interview, I would choose Python.
sentences.zh: 如果我可以选择面试语言，我会选择Python。

sentences.en: Partly because it’s a language I’m pretty well versed in, but also because I didn’t want to deal with memory issues in an algorithmic interview.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为这是我非常熟悉的语言，但也因为我不想在算法面试中处理内存问题。

blocks.html_en: Generally, I would recommend going for a high-level language that you are familiar with. There is little value in wrestling with the borrow checker or forgetting to declare a variable when you could just use Python and focus on the algorithm.

sentences.en: Generally, I would recommend going for a high-level language that you are familiar with.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，我建议选择您熟悉的高级语言。

sentences.en: There is little value in wrestling with the borrow checker or forgetting to declare a variable when you could just use Python and focus on the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 当您可以只使用 Python 并专注于算法时，与借用检查器搏斗或忘记声明变量没有什么价值。

blocks.html_en: There are many resources to prepare for these types of interviews, and getting good at them is pretty much a practice and pattern recognition thing. You build a repertoire of algorithmic techniques and useful data structures and their operations, and with time, develop expertise to mix and match to a solution quickly.

sentences.en: There are many resources to prepare for these types of interviews, and getting good at them is pretty much a practice and pattern recognition thing.
sentences.zh: 有很多资源可以为此类面试做准备，而做好这些面试很大程度上需要练习和模式识别。

sentences.en: You build a repertoire of algorithmic techniques and useful data structures and their operations, and with time, develop expertise to mix and match to a solution quickly.
sentences.zh: 您构建一系列算法技术和有用的数据结构及其操作，并随着时间的推移，开发专业知识以快速混合和匹配解决方案。

blocks.html_en: I found the Neetcode 150 roadmap particularly useful. It’s an ordered collection of LeetCode problems that one after the other introduce new and more advanced concepts. I found that much more useful than the arbitrary order of LeetCode.

sentences.en: I found the Neetcode 150 roadmap particularly useful.
sentences.zh: 我发现 Neetcode 150 路线图特别有用。

sentences.en: It’s an ordered collection of LeetCode problems that one after the other introduce new and more advanced concepts.
sentences.zh: 它是 LeetCode 问题的有序集合，一个接一个地引入新的、更高级的概念。

sentences.en: I found that much more useful than the arbitrary order of LeetCode.
sentences.zh: 我发现这比 LeetCode 的任意顺序有用得多。

blocks.html_en: Because I am a big believer in more rigorous (self-)education, I’ve also read Skiena’s Algorithm Design Manual. This is probably a bit too theoretical for immediate interview preparation, but it is a great base for your life as a programmer.

sentences.en: Because I am a big believer in more rigorous (self-)education, I’ve also read Skiena’s Algorithm Design Manual.
sentences.zh: 因为我坚信更严格的（自我）教育，所以我还阅读了 Skiena 的算法设计手册。

sentences.en: This is probably a bit too theoretical for immediate interview preparation, but it is a great base for your life as a programmer.
sentences.zh: 对于立即准备面试来说，这可能有点过于理论化，但它是您作为程序员的生活的良好基础。

blocks.html_en: For more conceptual coding interview preparation, I’ve supplemented this with reading Coding Interview Patterns — a practical and interview-focused approach to data structures and algorithms.

sentences.en: For more conceptual coding interview preparation, I’ve supplemented this with reading Coding Interview Patterns — a practical and interview-focused approach to data structures and algorithms.
sentences.zh: 对于更多概念性的编码面试准备，我通过阅读编码面试模式来补充这一点——这是一种实用且以面试为中心的数据结构和算法方法。

blocks.html_en: In the end, I’ve probably done around 300 LeetCode/NeetCode problems. About half of that is to build muscle memory, and then 20-30 rapid-fire questions in the days leading up to the coding interviews.

sentences.en: In the end, I’ve probably done around 300 LeetCode/NeetCode problems.
sentences.zh: 最后，我大概做了大约 300 道 LeetCode/NeetCode 题。

sentences.en: About half of that is to build muscle memory, and then 20-30 rapid-fire questions in the days leading up to the coding interviews.
sentences.zh: 其中大约一半是为了建立肌肉记忆，然后在编码面试前几天提出 20-30 个快速问题。

blocks.html_en: The interviews themselves consisted usually of two or three problems, with the first one or two being equivalent to a LeetCode easy as a warm-up, followed mostly by a LeetCode medium, though I’ve encountered hards.

sentences.en: The interviews themselves consisted usually of two or three problems, with the first one or two being equivalent to a LeetCode easy as a warm-up, followed mostly by a LeetCode medium, though I’ve encountered hards.
